profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: Parsons Avenue, Shadeville, Columbus, Hamilton Township, Franklin County, OH 43137
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's central Ohio data center footprint, mapped on Parsons Avenue in the Shadeville area of Columbus, Hamilton Township, Franklin County, near the company's Lockbourne-area operations. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within this footprint, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

Ohio's central corridor data center cluster, of which this Columbus-area building is part, has grown rapidly since 2019 alongside major campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Ohio footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google has mapped a data center building on Parsons Avenue in the Shadeville area of Columbus as part of its central Ohio campus, which spans New Albany, Lockbourne, and Lancaster. Google does not publish megawatt capacity or building-specific identifiers for individual structures within this footprint, so this site's address and location come from OpenStreetMap mapping rather than from Google's own public specifications. The building cannot be ranked by IT load or confirmed as a separate facility unit against Google's published materials.

This building sits within central Ohio's data center cluster, which has attracted Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services alongside Google since 2019, and which now represents one of the state's largest technology investment centers. American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) serves the region and has filed with state regulators for new tariff structures to handle growing data center demand. Google has invested more than $20 billion across its Ohio footprint and contributed to $21.7 billion in state economic activity in 2025, though this campus-level investment is not broken down by individual building.

Ohio's state and local tax abatement programs have anchored the central corridor's growth. Across Ohio, 76 data center facilities are mapped in this registry, of which only 8 publish megawatt figures totaling 60.4 MW, so this building's capacity contribution to the state's power demand cannot be read from published operator data. Whether this structure operates as a separate load unit, or as part of an aggregate campus load, is not published by Google.
